SteerBridge seeks a Product Designer to join our Experience Design team supporting our Aviation Tech team and the continued development and expansion of AIRES, our aviation readiness capability.
In this role, you will create high-fidelity UI prototypes in Figma, help maintain and extend our design system, and translate research findings, operational workflows, and technical requirements into clear, production-ready product experiences.
You will work as part of a small product design team, collaborating closely with a senior product designer who will provide day-to-day direction, design critique, and mentorship. You will also work with UX researchers, engineers, data teams, product stakeholders, and aviation subject-matter experts.
Ideal candidates are strong UI craftspeople who understand how design systems work in practice, are comfortable designing complex data-rich interfaces, are eager to learn, and thrive on clear direction and regular feedback. Over time, this role is expected to grow from executing defined design work to taking greater ownership of product workflows and features.
In data and software engineering, a design pattern is a battle-tested blueprint for solving a recurring problem. It is not a specific piece of code, but a standardized mental model that allows teams to skip the trial-and-error phase of architecture.
SteerBridge applies proven patterns such as Medallion Architecture to structure, validate, and operationalize data within mission-critical aviation analytics platforms.
Product designers work within this architectural context to translate complex data, workflows, and system behavior into clear, usable, and decision-ready experiences for operators working in high-consequence environments.
The platform supports aviation readiness and sustainment operations including:
Primary users include aviation maintainers, logisticians, planners, and senior decision-makers operating under time pressure and incomplete information.
The work involves complex, data-rich interfaces that help users understand aircraft status, maintenance requirements, supply constraints, readiness risk, and potential courses of action.
Design high-fidelity prototypes and production-ready interfaces in Figma, translating wireframes, user flows, UX research, operational requirements, and technical constraints into polished product experiences.
Design complex, data-driven workflows and interfaces supporting aviation readiness, maintenance, logistics, and operational planning.
Partner with UX researchers and aviation subject-matter experts to translate validated user needs, research findings, and operational workflows into wireframes, interaction models, prototypes, and product designs.
Support and maintain the team’s design system by applying established components, tokens, visual standards, and interaction patterns consistently and identifying opportunities for new or improved patterns.
Collaborate with engineers, product stakeholders, researchers, and data teams to evaluate design feasibility, refine solutions, and iterate based on usability testing, stakeholder feedback, technical constraints, and evolving requirements.
Prepare detailed design handoffs, including states, edge cases, interactions, and expected behaviors, and perform design QA to ensure implemented features align with Figma specifications.
Manage multiple design tasks and Jira tickets across sprints, working within established priorities, estimating work, tracking progress, and proactively communicating blockers.
Participate in design reviews and critiques, incorporate feedback into subsequent iterations, and clearly communicate design rationale to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

29b6cb31a810bcbd89ea1f8fb5c9adc8.description:
Our fully-remote team is spread across North America, Europe, and Asia, and includes alumni of remote-first organizations like 37Signals and GitHub. There is no “HQ” and we have no plans to open one.
You can read more about our philosophy and values here .
About the role
We’re hiring a UX Designer to own customer research and UX design at Workbrew.
This is a research-weighted role, and we mean that literally. Roughly half your time goes on talking to customers, testing ideas with them, and turning what you learn into recommendations the company acts on. The other half is the UX design work that follows from it: flows, prototypes, and the interface for a product that IT administrators live in every day.
We are a scaling company, one product team, and more bets to place than we can properly de-risk. We run product discovery continuously — every bet has a problem statement, a stated outcome, and a confidence level attached to it before we commit engineering time. What we want is more depth behind those decisions: more customers talked to, more ideas tested before they’re built, and evidence carried all the way through to a recommendation. That’s what this role owns.
Own customer research end to end: recruiting participants, writing user research scripts, moderating sessions, synthesizing, and writing recommendations.
Build static and interactive prototypes — putting them in front of real IT administrators before we commit engineering time to a specific direction.
Design parts of our web and native applications upfront, reducing the amount of time that we need to spend on “UX refactoring”.
Work with sales, customer success, and channel partner managers as your route to users — and then building your own relationships directly with those customers.
Describe how our segments actually differ between user personas and buyer types — so that we can focus on the right problems for the right people.
Decide and understand how much attention a given initiative deserves. Some things we know well enough to just build — some things we’re guessing at and need to test properly. Knowing the difference is the job.
Run our quantitative research: surveys, satisfaction and sentiment measurement, and unmoderated testing, so we hear from a lot more customers than we can get on a call.
Help set up and read quantitative product analytics, so we know whether what we shipped worked.
Product decisions cite evidence instead of assumptions, and everyone in the company can see the evidence.
Initiatives get reshaped or killed before engineering starts, not after.
Significant pieces of work have had some form of prototype in front of real customers before we commit a long cycle to it.
We can describe how IT administrators, security teams, developers, and managed service providers each experience the product, and we design for them differently.
We have a running read on customer satisfaction, and we can see it move.
Workbrew gets measurably better to use, and the pace of shipping doesn’t drop.
Requirements
Requirements
5+ years designing B2B software products that shipped and are in-market. We want to be able to go and look at what you built and hear what your part in it was.
You have run research end to end yourself, and it changed what got built. Not just “partnered with a research team”. Come prepared to walk us through one study in detail.
You work with numbers, not just interviews. Surveys, satisfaction tracking or unmoderated testing at scale, and you've measured your own designs after they shipped.
You build your own prototypes and test them with users. Figma prototypes, AI-assisted coded prototypes, whatever gets something testable in front of someone quickly.
You have been the only UX Designer on a product team. Embedded with engineers and a product manager, feeding a team that ships constantly, picking the right depth of process for each piece of work rather than running the same playbook every time.
Experience designing for DevTools, IT, fleet manageme

Synthesize findings into what people actually need, stated separately from what they asked for, with the evidence for each.
Design the solution: user journeys, wireframes, and prototypes that an engineer can build from without guessing.
Decide where a human has to sign off inside a workflow, and design that checkpoint into the product rather than bolting it on afterward.
Test designs with real users before code exists, not after.

Prototype with AI tools as a default, not a novelty. Know when the AI-native path saves real time and when it produces something you have to rebuild by hand anyway.
Hand off design work in a state an engineer can actually start from, and stay involved enough during the build to catch it when implementation drifts from the intent.

Moves from synthesis to a working prototype fast.

AI fluent: uses AI daily to research, synthesize, and prototype, and can tell good output from slop.
Comfortable working directly alongside engineers through build.
No minimum years required. We hire on the work.
On-site in New York, with client-site travel for discovery work.
A bachelor's degree is preferred and is not a requirement.
A public portfolio or case studies we can look at before we meet.
Experience designing AI-native workflows, including where a human checkpoint belongs.
Consulting, agency, or professional services experience with concurrent clients.
Comfort with lightweight front-end implementation.

The Role
We're hiring Product Designers to help shape how enterprises understand, govern, and trust their AI agents.
Geordie is building category-defining tooling for agent visibility, governance, and risk. The design challenge is real: AI agent behaviour is complex, often opaque, and the stakes for our customers are high.
Our design team is small today; you'll report into our Head of Product Design and join two Product Designers. We have three development teams, growing to five, and we believe design works best embedded. You'll join one of those teams as its designer, working alongside its engineers and customers every day. Because we're still early, you'll also help set the foundation everything else is built on: the design language, the component library, and the patterns we use across the product. Our design team also looks after Geordie's brand, so you'll help shape how we show up beyond the product too, making sure brand and product feel like one coherent experience.
Design here isn't a layer applied at the end. We ship multiple times a day, and we actively encourage designers to use AI agents to write code and get closer to the product. We don't have Product Managers; design and engineering partner directly to figure out what to build. Our engineers are deeply product-minded, close to customers, and want to solve the right problem rather than ship to spec. Together you'll define problems, shape scope, and own outcomes. If you've ever wanted to own something end to end, this is it.
We also move fast. We ship multiple times a day, and we actively encourage designers to use AI agents to write code and get closer to the product. If you've ever wanted to own something end to end, this is it.
What You'll Do
Own the end-to-end design of core product experiences, from early concept through to shipped and iterated.
Help build Geordie's design system with the rest of the design team; the tokens, components, patterns, and documentation that everyone relies on, shaped by what your team needs.
Contribute to Geordie's brand; helping evolve our visual language, illustration, and assets so the product and brand tell one story.
Lead customer discovery and research; running interviews, identifying patterns, and bringing customer insight into every design decision.
Work directly with customers to test your thinking early and close the loop between insight and shipped product.
Collaborate daily with engineers; pairing, reviewing, and increasingly using AI tools to prototype and contribute to the codebase yourself.
Contribute to product direction: you will be in the room where decisions are made, not handed a spec to execute.
Keep a strong point of view on what good design looks like in a security and governance product; clear, trustworthy, and built for expert users.
The most important thing is that you care deeply about customers and can move fast without losing quality. You are a strong practitioner; you can go from whiteboard to high-fidelity quickly, and you know when each is appropriate.
You are comfortable with ambiguity. We are Series A, the product is evolving, and the domain of AI agent governance is genuinely new. You find that energising, not unsettling.
You have strong opinions about design systems and component architecture, and experience building or significantly contributing to one. You can articulate why decisions were made and defend them clearly.
You work well in a collaborative engineering culture. You are comfortable pair-designing with engineers, reviewing pull requests for design quality, and using AI tools to accelerate your own work.
Requirements
Significant experience as a product designer, with a portfolio that demonstrates complex UX problem-solving; not just polished visuals.
Experience designing highly complex B2B SaaS products, including data visualisation and data-dense interfaces; you can turn large volumes of information into something expert users can understand and act on.

082f09f57aa89b3997c8d24cb34774f0.title: UX Researcher
082f09f57aa89b3997c8d24cb34774f0.description:
HeyMilo Labs | Remote | Independent Contractor | $40–$100 per hour
HeyMilo Labs is looking for experienced UX researchers to participate in paid, recorded conversations with other research professionals. You’ll discuss research decisions, debate methodologies, and explain how you interpret evidence and communicate findings.
These conversations will help train and evaluate AI systems.
What you’ll do
Discuss research planning, participant recruitment, interview techniques, usability testing, and synthesis.
Debate which research approach fits a particular question, timeline, or product decision.
Defend an interpretation of fictional research findings while acknowledging limitations and uncertainty.
Challenge assumptions, probe alternative explanations, and respond to another researcher’s critique.
Explore how to communicate findings when stakeholders disagree or the evidence is incomplete.
Professional experience in UX research, user research, human factors, or a comparable research role.
Hands-on experience designing and conducting studies and communicating findings.
Fluent spoken communication in the language of the session.
The ability to distinguish observations from interpretations and support your perspective with evidence.
Comfort with a substantive, unscripted discussion that includes constructive disagreement.
Professional acting experience is optional. Domain expertise and conversational ability are essential.
Following an initial screening, selected applicants will be invited to a paid, recorded conversation with another research professional who has a similar background. You’ll discuss a topic within your shared expertise, debate research choices, and challenge each other’s interpretations.
Pay is $40–$100 per hour. The rate, expected time commitment, and recording-use and licensing terms will be shared before you accept an assignment. Recordings may be licensed to AI developers for training and evaluation under the agreed terms.
You’ll need a quiet environment, reliable internet, a clear microphone, and a webcam. Be comfortable appearing on video with your face visible and filters and background blur turned off. Use fictional or anonymized research examples.
Share your research background, methods and subject areas, availability, time zone, and spoken languages.

For the longest time, banking* has only really served one purpose, holding money securely. In doing so, it’s also slowed us down and overcomplicated things. That’s where Mercury comes in. Banking should do more and we’re on a mission to make that happen through powerful banking solutions and simplifying all of the financial workflows that come with managing a business. To accomplish this end, we also need to ensure the trust and safety of our customers, partners and ecosystem. Thankfully, Mercury has a world class Risk team to detect and mitigate any threats. And this team is growing. We’re looking to bring on a Risk User Experience Specialist to make risk decisions in response to risk-related user inquiries, all while providing best-in-class user experiences.
As a Risk User Experience Specialist, you’ll be responsible for responding to transaction limit request increases, making risk decisions on queued payments and check deposits, and leveraging your general risk knowledge to escalate unusual or high risk behavior to relevant teams. You’ll be responsible for providing great user experiences to Mercury users while making highly efficient and high quality risk assessments. You will report directly to the Risk User Experience Lead and will be supported by a highly functional team.
* Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Product Design team defines and delivers user-facing experiences across Stripe. Product Designers work closely with engineers, product managers, researchers, strategists, operations, data scientists, and marketers to shape products from early strategy through launch and iteration. You’ll be joining the Risk team, which shapes how businesses get started on Stripe, build trust, stay compliant, and grow with confidence. The work spans businesses of every size and helps keep both our users and Stripe’s ecosystem safe. Risk is a high-impact design space where the problems are both strategic and complex. As a designer on the team, you’ll help bring clarity to critical user moments, reduce friction for legitimate businesses, and raise the craft bar where trust, ease, and confidence matter most. This role is a strong fit for a designer who is energized by complexity, motivated by impact, and excited to turn difficult systems into simple, intuitive experiences.

What you’ll do
In this role, you’ll design experiences that help businesses start and grow successfully on Stripe. You’ll work closely with cross-functional partners to define problems, shape direction, and ship high-quality experiences.
Responsibilities
Translate complex systems, policies, and operational constraints into clear, thoughtful product experiences
Identify high-leverage opportunities that improve coherence across journeys, touchpoints, and surfaces
Partner closely with PMs, engineers, researchers, operations, and strategists to shape product direction and drive user and business outcomes
Develop both long-term strategy and pragmatic short-term solutions
Design, prototype, and communicate ideas with creative storytelling and demos
Use qualitative and quantitative signals to inform decisions and evaluate impact
Work closely with engineering to ensure a high bar for craft and implementation quality
Contribute to shared patterns and systems that help the broader Risk organization build with coherence
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
4+ years of relevant product design experience at a product-driven technology company
A portfolio demonstrating strong visual craft, interaction design, and systems thinking
Experience working on complex product areas with multiple stakeholders, constraints, and interconnected workflows
Strong product thinking and the ability to shape direction, not just execute against requirements
Demonstrated ability to prototype and design across multiple touchpoints and surfaces
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence through clear design rationale and artifacts
You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:
Think in systems and design solutions that scale across users, workflows, and surfaces
Have strong product judgment and influence beyond the UI
Care deeply about quality from concept through implementation
Are comfortable operating in fast-moving environments where priorities may shift in response to policy, operational, or regulatory needs

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.
About the Role
Everything at Verkada begins with design. Every part of our product experience is carefully crafted to be simple, elegant, and powerful. As a Product Designer, you will be responsible for delivering best-in-class web and mobile tools (user interface designs, interaction models, prototypes, etc.) in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. You’ll work with product managers, designers, and engineers to design our software, from defining a product vision to tweaking pixels before each release.
What You'll Do
Collaborate closely with designers, engineers, and product managers in a highly agile development environment with quick ideation and prototyping.
Build and foster a collaborative work environment.
Run inspiring and formal brainstorming sessions with engineers, product, and other designers.
Developing product strategies that deliver on customer needs and the company’s vision
Build clear, concise and intuitive UX/UI with everything from low-fidelity wireframes to pixel perfect final designs.
Serve as a project lead, co-owning the final product with product and engineering leads.
Manage multiple projects and stakeholder relationships.
Manage and maintain a project’s scope and schedule.
Initiate and participate in user research as needed on key projects.
3+ years of product design or mobile product design experience
Polished portfolio that demonstrates strong visual and interaction design skills
Bachelor's degree in design, art, human-computer interaction (HCI), or equivalent
A drive to solve complex problems with simple and elegant solutions
Proven experience in creative problem solving and partnering with product, engineering, and other designers to do so
Experienced in creating and integrating animated visuals and interactive design
Proficient in: Figma, Adobe Creative Suite (PhotoShop, After Effects, and Illustrator)

e243719a09d34066462299cb6809a246.title: UX Researcher II
e243719a09d34066462299cb6809a246.description:
Guides Product Managers and Designers in conducting their own user research, including recommending the right methodologies for specific initiatives and sharing best practices.
Help standup and run measurement programs like NPS.
Support vendor management and research operations. Evaluate new vendor features worth adopting.
Educational and Experience Requirements
2-4 years of UX research experience in a product development environment, ideally B2B SaaS or other complex products, with a portfolio or case studies that show studies you owned, how you told the story, and the decisions it informed.
Excellent reading, writing, and speaking skills. You absorb dense technical, quantitative, and qualitative information, simplify it without losing accuracy, and tell a clear, compelling story that supports sound decisions. You also push back respectfully and use evidence to help a team align.
Proven experience collaborating with product managers, designers, and engineers.
Working knowledge of usability and mixed methods, with a clear approach to data analysis and measurement.
Experience using AI tools in research, and a critical eye for hallucinations, unsupported claims, and weak reasoning. You verify before you share.
Demonstrated proficiency in using industry-standard UX research tools, like Great Question, UserTesting, Dovetail, Qualtrics, Pendo.
Exposure to B2B marketing, sales, or martech products. We will help you learn the domain.
Designs clear, efficient studies built around research goals and questions. Ensures research studies will yield actionable insights.
Analyzes data using industry standards and statistics.
Clearly connects research insights to overarching UX vision.
Proficiency in survey design, including question wording, response scales, and techniques for reducing bias.
Excellent communication skills whether writing, speaking informally, or presenting at all levels of the organization.
Humility, adaptability, and teachability, shown in how you seek feedback, admit what you do not know, and adjust to change.
Collaborative across disciplines and teams and takes a proactive approach to drive positive product outcomes.
Plays an active role in providing feedback to peers to shape research studies.
Comfort with ambiguity, and a track record of creating clarity through organized communication, documentation, and operations.
Comfort with fast sprint cycles, several projects at once, and asynchronous work with a distributed team.
Proactively adapts to changing tooling and workflows to find more efficient and effective ways of working.

At Arlo, we're passionate about creating innovative and reliable solutions that help people protect what matters most to them. Our team is dedicated to delivering products that exceed our customers' expectations, while always pushing the boundaries of what's possible in the world of protection technology. We believe that everyone deserves to feel safe and secure, whether they're at home or away, and we're committed to providing our customers with the peace of mind they need to live their lives without worry. Arlo’s deep expertise in AI- and CV-powered analytics, cloud services, user experience, product design, and innovative wireless and RF connectivity enables the delivery of a seamless, smart security experience for Arlo users that is easy to set up and interact with every day.
About the role
The UX Design Operations Coordinator is a six-month contract role supporting Arlo's User Experience organization. This role helps the UX team operate efficiently and maintain clear visibility across a portfolio of software, hardware, and service experiences. The coordinator will partner closely with Design leadership, designers, Product Management, Engineering, Program Management, and other business partners to keep priorities, resources, timelines, dependencies, decisions, and deliverables aligned.
This is a highly collaborative, detail-oriented role for someone who enjoys bringing structure to complex work, improving team processes, and keeping projects moving. The role is focused on operational excellence rather than visual design execution.
·   Partner with UX Design leadership to coordinate the team's project portfolio, priorities, capacity, and key deliverables across mobile, web, hardware, and platform experiences.
·   Maintain project plans, schedules, milestones, status, dependencies, risks, and action items; proactively surface issues that could affect delivery.
·   Coordinate design resourcing across projects and help leadership identify capacity gaps, competing priorities, and opportunities to rebalance work.
·   Provide clear, concise project and portfolio visibility for stakeholders, including regular updates on priorities, resource utilization, milestones, risks, and decisions.
·   Act as an operational bridge between Design, Product Management, Engineering, Program Management, and other cross-functional partners to ensure dependencies and handoffs are understood and managed.
·   Own or facilitate the UX design intake process, helping teams capture requests, clarify scope and timing, assess priority, and route work appropriately.
·   Identify opportunities to improve UX workflows, tools, documentation, asset management, and team rituals; help implement practical changes that increase efficiency and reduce friction.
·   Coordinate key design reviews, planning sessions, workshops, and leadership meetings, including agendas, materials, action items, and follow-through.
·   Connect related work across products, features, platforms, and initiatives; identify potential collisions, duplicated effort, or gaps and work with partners to resolve them.
·   Support quarterly and annual planning by consolidating project commitments, resource needs, timelines, and operational risks into a clear view for UX leadership and business partners.
·   Help maintain operational systems and reporting used by the UX organization, including project trackers, planning tools, documentation, and shared team resources.
·   Bring together business goals, customer needs, technology, design intent, and execution realities so teams can make informed decisions and keep work progressing.
·   Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
·   Experience in design operations, design program management, project management, agency operations, or a closely related role.
·   Experience working with creative or UX teams and an understanding of how to introduce useful process and structure without slowing creative work.
·   Strong project management skills, i

Experience applying user-centered design methods and translating user, technical, and business requirements into digital-product designs.

About the Role
Neighbor is a two-sided marketplace for self storage and vehicle storage. Hosts list everything from garages and driveways to RV pads and commercial facility units, and renters compare options, book, and manage reservations through Neighbor’s website and apps.
You’ll report directly to a Co-Founder and our VP of Product & Design, and you’ll set the bar for design craft across the company. That means mentoring Neighbor’s other designers, shaping product direction with PMs and engineers from the first sketch, and making sure real renter insight reaches every team. Renters on Neighbor compare everything from storage facility units to neighborhood garages and RV pads. Helping them choose with confidence is a hard design problem, and solving it moves the business directly.
This role is based in our Lehi, Utah office, in person Tuesday through Friday, with the option to work from home on Mondays.
Own end-to-end design across iOS, Android, and responsive web, from problem framing through ship and measurement
Run renter and host research (interviews, usability tests, session and funnel reviews) and turn it into recommendations the team acts on

Co-define success metrics with PM and Eng, design experiments, and iterate on what the data shows
Align early with wireframes and prototypes (including AI and code-assisted) so ideas get in front of users in days, not weeks
Design trust and clarity into every surface: pricing, photos, reviews, access details, and host and renter information
Cover the full journey: every state, edge case, and platform convention, so defects rarely reach production
Evolve the Neighbor design and brand system so every surface feels like one product
Mentor Neighbor’s designers through critique, pairing, and hands-on feedback

2+ years of product design (UX/UI), with shipped work on native iOS, Android, and responsive web
A portfolio showing consumer flows you owned end to end and the results they drove
Excellent visual and interaction craft suited to a consumer marketplace
You plan and run your own interviews and usability tests
You read funnels and A/B results and use them to make design decisions
Expert in Figma, and you use AI tools regularly for research, exploration, and prototyping
A clear writer and presenter who can defend a decision to a co-founder or an engineer
You own outcomes, not just tasks, and you actively seek hard feedback and act on it
Able to work in our Lehi, Utah office Tuesday through Friday (remote work isn’t an option for this role)
Experience with two-sided marketplaces, e-commerce, or travel and booking products
Has mentored designers or led design for a team
Startup experience, or time as a solo designer who owned the whole problem
Comfortable building working prototypes in code or with AI coding tools

Build trust with users through deep empathy, active listening, and strong facilitation, enabling a thorough understanding of their goals, workflows, and challenges.

Mentor and provide feedback to less experienced designers and researchers, sharing methods and best practices across the team.

1e539fe9661fdbfcc29563a84c527ed9.description:
Apollo supports some of the largest GraphQL APIs in the world. Companies like Walmart, Expedia, Peloton, DoorDash, and The New York Times are just a small sample of our customers. And what consumes an API is changing: increasingly it’s an agent acting on someone’s behalf, one that needs a graph it can traverse and controls over what it can reach. That’s the next thing we’re building, and design will decide whether it’s usable.
About the role
Apollo assigns designers to our highest-leverage problems, and priorities are set quarterly. Current areas include developer onboarding, our core product interfaces, the design system, and emerging agentic products.
You’ll work alongside our Head of Design, owning well-scoped problem areas end to end: understanding the users and the system behind them, shaping a v1 with engineering, and shipping polished, usable experiences. You’ll bring a point of view to your work and help raise the craft bar across the team.
What you’ll do
Own design for defined workflows in our developer tools, from discovery through shipped experience.
Partner day to day with engineers and PMs to shape what gets built, and bring a point of view on scope and trade-offs.
Scope v1s that deliver value quickly, then iterate based on usage and feedback.
Design for the details that make technical products trustworthy: states, edge cases, errors, and permissions.
Contribute reusable patterns and components to our design system, and help migrate product surfaces onto it.
Use AI tools to prototype and test ideas quickly, and run lightweight usability tests when the cost of being wrong is high.
Tie your work to outcomes such as task completion, developer activation, or fewer support tickets from confusing flows.
Who you are
Minimum requirements
5+ years designing software, with a focus on product or UX design.
Experience designing complex products, ideally for technical users: developer tools, infrastructure, data, security, identity, or APIs.
A track record of owning features or workflows end to end, from discovery through shipping.
Strong visual design, interaction, and craft skills.
Comfortable working through ambiguity within a defined problem area.
Preferred qualifications
Have shipped developer-focused experiences, API tooling, or agent experiences.
Experience contributing to a design system, and knowing when to work outside it.
Use AI tools to prototype and explore ideas faster.
An engineering background, or comfort working in code.
Equally comfortable thinking through a whole user journey and sweating the interaction details.
Apollo helps teams build, operate, and scale the graphs that power modern applications. If you’ve streamed a show, booked a trip, or read the news online, there’s a good chance Apollo was working quietly behind the scenes. We support some of the largest and most sophisticated GraphQL platforms in the world.
But we’re not here just to maintain the status quo. Apollo is redefining how software teams build and ship - bringing clarity, speed, and leverage to increasingly complex systems. Our platform gives teams a single, coherent way to connect clients, services, and now AI-powered experiences, without drowning in endpoints or bespoke integrations.
Just as importantly, we’re building a company where ambitious people can do the best work of their careers. Just as importantly, you’ll write and refine UX copy for core member experiences, such as care plan screens and AI agent intro and onboarding screens.

You will partner directly with Engineering, who owns prompts and configuration, as well as Clinical and Product to bring a single, consistent point of view on voice, tone, taxonomy and language, and to hold a high bar for usability, clinical integrity, clarity, and the right amount of empathy in a health context.

Write and refine UX copy for in-product experiences such as care plan screens, AI agent intro and onboarding screens, navigation and CTAs, empty and error states, and in-app education
Craft language that is empowering and action-oriented, balancing clinical accuracy and compliance with a human, non-alarming Maven-branded tone
Work within design systems and with product designers to balance copy density, hierarchy, and usability
Name products, features, programs, and agents as needed, using a structured approach to generating, screening, and recommending names with rationale
Work closely and directly with the Member Copy, Comms & Content team, clinicians, product managers, designers, and engineers
Expected to attend weekly check-in meetings; as well as brainstorm sessions as needed

e948f693e02c84315b5f80f1e4bbae54.description:
RainFocus cares about its employees, customers, and the world in which we live. Our rapidly growing team serves Fortune 500 companies like Adobe, Cisco, IBM, Oracle, VMware, and others to prepare and execute in-person, virtual, and hybrid events, across the world. Those events are delivered through our industry-disrupting software platform, with groundbreaking business intelligence, to elevate the attendee experience, streamline event operations, and accelerate marketing results. We are well-funded, growing fast, and building a company that is changing the market — it will be challenging, fun and exciting.
About the Role
You’ll play an important part in the entire product development process, from brainstorming to launch. You’ll be part of a UX team where each designer is responsible for different areas of our product and integrated into individual scrum teams. They work closely with the Product Manager and Developers to create elegant solutions to problems our customers are facing. The product team also includes front-end developers who share our passion to deliver a great user experience throughout our platform.
What You'll Do:
Partner with stakeholders and executives to capture strategic ideas and turn them into clear hypotheses
Define the problem, the target customer, the business case, and the evidence that would change our minds
Push back constructively when an idea lacks a clear problem or buyer
Plan and run high-volume discovery with customers and prospects, including interviews, workshops, concept tests, and usability sessions
Work with Stakeholders, Sales, and Customer Success to find the right participants quickly
Synthesize findings into short, decision-ready insights
Create interactive prototypes, from clickable concepts to functional PoCs, using AI-assisted tools
Apply sound UX judgment to flows, information architecture, and interaction design
Work with your developer counterpart to draw a clear line between prototype-grade and production-ready, and hand off cleanly
Use PoCs to confirm understanding, not to deliver solutions
Test willingness to adopt and pay, not just whether people like the idea
Define success signals before each validation cycle and track them
Present recommendations to leadership with the evidence behind them
Frame every prototype clearly as exploratory so customers never hear a commitment
Work with Sales and Legal on NDAs, disclosure, and expectation-setting
Keep Sales informed of what you're learning and what is, and isn't, safe to say to customers
Set priorities, rhythm, and working agreements for a small cross-functional team
Share frequent, brief readouts instead of big-bang reviews
Build reusable templates, scripts, and prototype patterns that make each cycle faster
Build or customize solutions for a specific customer
Help customers integrate, configure, or implement our software
Make roadmap or delivery commitments based purely on a PoC
Ship production code (engineering reviews and rebuilds PoCs before anything goes to market)
Success is measured by the quality of the decision, not by whether an idea moves forward. A well-evidenced "stop" is a win.
Ideas reach a go/no-go decision in weeks, not quarters
Ideas the business funds are backed by clear problem definitions, working prototypes, and customer proof
Leadership and Sales trust the evidence and understand why ideas advanced or stopped
Fewer fully built features fail to find demand
Strong business thinking: markets, buyers, pricing, and ROI, not just usability
Demonstrated rapid prototyping ability, including fluency with AI-assisted building tools
Hands-on discovery research experience and comfort talking directly with customers and prospects, including senior stakeholders
UX and product design fundamentals, with a portfolio or examples of shipped work

0c60ec52411cba6da0173dbe0fbe9e89.title: UX/UI Researcher
0c60ec52411cba6da0173dbe0fbe9e89.description:
Yaqeen is a nonprofit on a mission to pioneer Islamic research in creative, cutting-edge formats tailored to meet people where they are. We work to dismantle doubts through well-researched truths, nurture conviction by strengthening belief with practical, spiritual guidance, and inspire contribution by reviving our tradition of faithful changemakers, insha’Allah . We’re seeking like-minded professionals who embody Islamic values including sincerity, excellence, and compassion, and want to make a difference in the faith of people worldwide.
What You'll Do
Yaqeen Institute for Islamic Research creates research papers, articles, videos, ebooks and learning curricula for Muslims around the world, from people exploring faith to educators and community leaders who share our work. We’re looking for a UX/UI researcher to help our product teams understand how people discover, use and value these products, and to bring that understanding into how we design and improve them.
The first project focuses on our free library of English-language ebooks. Our last in-depth study of these readers was in 2024, and reading habits and search tools, including AI assistants, have changed a lot since then. A reader survey is already running, and this project goes deeper through one-on-one interviews. You will own the study end to end, from research questions to synthesis. Your findings will shape the library’s product roadmap and help Yaqeen measure the value it creates for readers.
This is a four-month contract that may be extended or converted into a longer-term, full-time role.
For the ebook library, review the 2024 research and early results from the current reader survey, and work with the Product Manager to set the study's research questions and objectives.
Write a discussion guide that ties each research question to the outcomes the product team tracks, such as downloads, how readers discover the library, and whether consuming a product leads them on to Yaqeen's research and other content.
Screen and recruit a mix of participants across reader segments, by drawing on survey respondents who opt in to follow-up interviews.
Run and record one-on-one interviews with ebook readers that explore:
what readers do after they finish a book (for example, read further, share it, apply it, or move to other Yaqeen content)
how they prefer to read and listen (PDF, EPUB, audiobook, print, on phone or on desktop)
how the way they search for and research Islamic topics has changed over the past few years, including any use of AI tools
which features they would find useful on the library's website and in the reading experience
the topics they want Yaqeen to write about next
Synthesize the findings, compare them against the 2024 research, and show what has held steady, what has shifted, and what is new.
Deliver a written findings report on the ebook library and present a readout to stakeholders, with prioritized recommendations for the product, editorial and marketing teams.
Handle participant data with care: get informed consent, collect only what the study needs, anonymize personal details in all notes and reports, and honor any request to change or delete a participant's data.
Help measure the impact of Yaqeen's products on users' religiosity using BASIC, Yaqeen's religiosity framework, for example by building its measures into surveys and discussion guides and tracking change over time.
Share research methods, templates and findings with other product teams, and advise on where user research could inform their roadmaps.
Help set up research practices other teams can reuse, such as a participant panel, standard consent forms and a shared library of findings.
Qualifications & Required Skills
A bachelor's degree in human-computer interaction, psychology, sociology, anthropology, information science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. A master's degree or formal research training is a plus.
Experience planning and running qualitative user resear

Job Description
At Agilent, you'll help transform the laboratories that are advancing life-changing therapies and expanding our understanding of biological systems. As a UX Designer on our global UX team, you'll create intuitive software and connected workflows that enable scientists to focus on discovery, not technology.
This unique role spans Cell Analysis and next-generation Laboratory Automation, offering the opportunity to shape the software experiences scientists use today while helping define the intelligent, automated laboratories of the future. Based in the Santa Clara area, you'll collaborate closely with scientists, product managers, software engineers, and automation experts across Agilent's global organization.
Design intuitive software experiences for Cell Analysis instruments, applications, and scientific workflows.
Develop a deep understanding of cellular analysis workflows and user needs to create scientifically grounded, user-centered solutions.
Translate scientific, technical, business, and user requirements into workflows, prototypes, and intuitive interfaces.
Help create a seamless experience across software, instruments, and user touchpoints.
Partner with UX researchers and stakeholders to evaluate concepts and improve usability.
Conduct UX research to understand how scientists and laboratory teams work today and how automation will shape future workflows.
Map end-to-end laboratory processes, identifying pain points, opportunities, dependencies, and automation needs.
Engage customers and internal experts through interviews, observations, and workshops to uncover insights.
Translate research findings into workflow models, recommendations, and opportunity areas that guide product strategy.
Collaborate with scientists, automation specialists, product managers, and development teams to ensure solutions are grounded in real-world needs.
Validate concepts with users and refine solutions before implementation.
Advocate for the user perspective in cross-functional discussions and decision-making.
Partner with Product Management, Engineering, and UX teams throughout discovery, design, development, and validation.
Apply and contribute to Agilent's design system to create consistent, scalable experiences.
Leverage modern AI-powered design and prototyping tools to accelerate innovation and communication.
Help shape the future of connected, intelligent laboratory software that empowers scientists worldwide.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master's degree in UX Design, Interaction Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Human Factors, or a related field.
3+ years of UX design experience in life sciences, laboratory software, medical technology, enterprise software, or other complex technical environments.
Experience conducting qualitative UX research and translating findings into actionable product insights.
Strong skills in workflow design, interaction design, information architecture, prototyping, and UI design.
Proficiency with Figma and modern design tools.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills with cross-functional teams.
Preferred Qualifications

About the Team
The Intelligence and Investigations (I2) team provides intelligence to decision makers across OpenAI and investigates severe misuse of our products. I2’s work saves lives: we disrupt real-world violence, protect children, and prevent catastrophic harms from AI misuse. We draw on our investigations and in-depth analysis of a wide range of data sources to provide actionable quantitative and qualitative intelligence to OpenAI’s leadership.

Our analysts and investigators make sense of complex data to understand emerging risks and investigate severe misuse. They work closely with engineers who build tools that extend what human experts can see and do. The design of the investigative workflow shapes how effectively people can use those tools and act on what they learn.
About the Role
We’re hiring a service designer to shape how investigative cases move through OpenAI, from the first signal through review and action. You’ll work alongside investigators to understand what each case requires and how the overall workflow shapes what investigators can accomplish.

You’ll bring that perspective to the people who shape investigative operations and the engineers who build the underlying systems. Together, you’ll decide where a change would help and see how it works in real cases.

In this role, you will
Work alongside investigators to understand how cases move across teams and systems. Consider what that process means for people at risk, people whose activity is under review, and the people responsible for acting on a finding.

Combine what you learn from individual cases with operational data to decide where a change would help most and whether it calls for a change in the workflow, the tools, or both.

Lead the cross-team work of mapping investigative workflows, designing improvements with the people who use and operate them, and putting agreed changes into practice.

Guide engineering decisions about how investigative systems fit together to support the overall workflow.

Follow changes into use. Look for whether they help investigators act in time, make well-supported decisions, and sustain demanding work.

We're seeking someone with experience including:
8+ years of relevant experience in service design or closely related roles, with demonstrated ownership of improvements to complex operational workflows from research through implementation and evaluation.

A bachelor’s degree in Service Design, Interaction Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Human Factors, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Strong qualitative research and synthesis skills, with the ability to combine insights from investigators and analysts with operational data to identify bottlenecks, inform priorities, and improve decision-making.

Experience designing across internal tools, SME workflows, and systems, including how information, evidence, and decisions move between teams.

Proven experience leading ambiguous projects across product, engineering, operations, and policy teams, translating evolving risks and needs into practical solutions.

Experience using AI tools to support research synthesis, explore service design options, and prototype workflows, with sound judgment about sensitive information, output validation, and decisions that require human review.

Clear written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to make complex workflows understandable, explain design decisions, navigate tradeoffs, and build alignment across technical and operational teams.

A hands-on approach and the persistence to follow improvements through rollout, adoption, and evaluation, measuring their effect on investigation quality, timeliness, and team effectiveness.

You might thrive in this role if you
Have experience designing services around the needs of the people who use and run them.

Enjoy learning how specialists work. You can draw on their different perspectives to understand a service that no single team sees in full.

3c461d107d8ce58470c2fbffce782fa8.title: Founding Designer
3c461d107d8ce58470c2fbffce782fa8.description:
The Problem
The most common design pattern for enterprise software assumes a human is doing the work. At Fragment, an agent is. We're fascinated by the gap between what procurement software is and what it could be.
Fragment is a platform where enterprise teams hand real work to AI agents: matching invoices, resolving change orders, catching duplicate payments across ERPs, moving millions of dollars through procurement workflows that used to require entire departments. The agents already run production workflows for Fortune 500 companies. What they'll be able to do in two, five, ten years, nobody knows yet, and the interface has to be designed for that. When does the agent just act? When does it pause and ask? How does a person see what happened, why, and whether to trust it? How do you give someone confidence in work they didn't do themselves?

Why Procurement
Because the stakes are real and the opportunity is wide open. Every $1B+ company has procurement, AP, and operations teams who spend their entire day inside their tools. These teams run the operational core of every large company, yet the software was never designed for them. The gap between what exists and what's possible is the biggest we've seen in enterprise software, and it's the reason customers found us with $0 in marketing and are now referring us to their networks.

What You'll Own
You will own the design of the Fragment platform: onboarding, connecting systems of record, defining agents, configuring workflows, monitoring them in production. Flows, wireframes, high-fidelity UI, and the design system that holds it together as the product grows.
Design how humans and agents work together. Decide what agents surface, when a person steps in, and how every decision stays visible and auditable. This is the core of the product and the part of the industry that hasn't been figured out.

Make dense things feel simple. Take a failed 3-way match or a change order after goods receipt and turn it into something a person can understand at a glance. You'll care as much about how a workflow is structured as how it looks.

Know the customer cold. Sit with procurement and finance leaders, join customer sessions with our Agent Strategists, and design from how their teams actually work rather than how we imagine they do.

Ship with engineering. Prototype fast, scope with the team, iterate on real usage. Small team, high trust.

Define what agentic procurement looks like. The category is finally getting modern software, but nobody has shown what it looks like when agents do the work. Our decks, product visuals, and customer-facing materials are a chance to set that bar in public, and you'll have the room to do it.

Who You Are
You have 5+ years of product design experience.

You have a portfolio of enterprise or B2B work that made complex tools feel intuitive.

You've turned messy business processes into clear mental models.

You've shipped, not just mocked.

You're comfortable being the only designer in the room and would rather own the whole problem than a slice of it.

Nice to Have
Experience with agentic or AI-native products

Experience building or scaling a design system

Early or founding designer at a startup

Experience creating sales and marketing collateral

Familiarity with procurement, finance, or ERP software

Who You'd Be Working With
A CEO who scaled three Zoom products past $300M in revenue, a CTO who has spent his career in enterprise AI, and a team that includes repeat founders, Caltech PhDs, former quants, chess masters, and one very enthusiastic Bonsai grower. 30x revenue growth in the first half of this year, nearly all of it from customer references.

Reach out even if you're not sure you're a perfect fit. Send a portfolio, we'd love to see it.

About Qualitate
Qualitate is building the AI-native primary intelligence platform for enterprises, investment firms, and asset managers. We automate the entire primary research workflow, from study design and expert recruitment through AI-moderated interviews and insight synthesis - replacing weeks of manual research with hours of high-signal output.
Expert research is a broken industry dominated by legacy incumbents with expensive, manual, and slow services. Investment and corporate strategy teams spend hundreds of hours coordinating intermediaries, scheduling expert calls, and synthesizing insights across fragmented providers. The process takes weeks to produce short-lived intelligence.
Qualitate transforms this workflow by autonomously conducting expert discussions at scale using AI. Qualitate’s AI Moderator interviews thousands of experts simultaneously each month, capturing forward-looking purchasing plans, competitive displacement, and real-time ROI signals. The platform turns these interviews into quantified, time-series outputs tracking over 10,000 public and private companies, queryable instantly in natural language. Our customers include some of the world’s largest enterprises, hedge funds, PE firms, credit investors, and venture capital firms.
The Role
We’re looking for a Product Designer to shape how organizations conduct research, explore evidence, and make decisions with AI. You’ll bring strong interaction design, visual craft, and product judgment to workflows that must feel clear and trustworthy, even when the underlying information is complex.
You’ll work closely with product, engineering, and design teammates from early exploration through launch and iteration. Along the way, you’ll help evolve the patterns, prototypes, and research practices that enables Qualitate’s vision of building the future of always-on continuous intelligence.

What the day-to-day looks like:
Turn research questions into usable workflows. Design how people move through complex tasks, keeping the next step clear as they gather information, explore findings, and reach decisions.

Make AI workflows understandable. Help users move from research questions to evidence and decisions, with clear ways to guide automation, inspect results, and stay in control.

Prototype to learn quickly. Rapidly build realistic prototypes to explore interaction ideas, test assumptions with users, and work through technical constraints with engineering.

Make complexity manageable for organizations. Design collaboration permissions, and administration so teams can work together while understanding who can see and do what.

Help decide what we build. Partner with product and engineering to identify opportunities, challenge assumptions, and make thoughtful tradeoffs between user needs, business goals, and implementation effort.

Strengthen the design system . Evolve reusable components and interaction patterns that make the product more cohesive and help the team ship faster.

Let customer evidence shape the roadmap . Work with product and engineering to turn research, feedback, and usage patterns into priorities, and revisit decisions when new evidence changes the picture.

Who This Role Is For
Experience shipping commercial products. You have 5+ years of product design experience, with a portfolio that shows your contribution to shipped work, the decisions behind it, and what you learned.

Strong interaction and visual craft. You can make complex workflows feel approachable and carry a design through its detailed interactions, product states, and visual execution.

Experience with complex software. You’ve designed for B2B or enterprise products and understand how different roles, information needs, and organizational constraints shape an experience.

Independent product judgement. You can frame an ambiguous problem, explore different approaches, and help decide what is worth building. You know when to move quickly and where more care or validation is needed.

AI agents are changing how enterprises operate. Companies want to move fast with MCPs and agents, but they need a way to do it safely.
CodeIntegrity is the platform security teams use to control MCPs and agents, built for companies deploying AI across the enterprise. We raised $5 million from SYN Ventures, Antler, and Boost, and we are a small team, mostly engineers, shipping fast. We are building the infrastructure that will make enterprise AI safe to use.
What You Will Do
You'll design the product security and engineering teams use to understand and control AI agents. Own the experience from the first sketch to the shipped interface, making complex activity, permissions, and security decisions easy to navigate and act on.
Start with the user's problem. Talk with customers, understand how they investigate activity and manage policies, and turn what you learn into clear design priorities.
Own complete workflows. Design onboarding, agent inventory, activity investigations, and policy configuration. Help users understand what an agent did, why an action was flagged or blocked, and what they can do next.
Make detailed interfaces feel simple. Bring clear information hierarchy, thoughtful interactions, and polished visual design to tables, filters, dashboards, and forms. Write interface copy that explains actions and their consequences.
Prototype and test ideas. Use Figma and interactive prototypes to explore alternatives with engineers and customers. Validate whether people can complete key tasks, then improve the design using feedback and product data.
Build reusable patterns. Maintain components and interaction guidelines that keep the product consistent and accessible. Design for keyboard use, different screen sizes, and loading, empty, and error states.
Stay involved through release. Work with engineers on technical constraints and implementation details, review the working product, and follow up on usability issues after launch.
What We Need
You've designed and shipped web applications, with a portfolio that explains the problem, your contribution, design decisions, and what you learned from the result.
You have strong visual and interaction design skills, including typography, layout, information hierarchy, and navigation.
You can turn complex workflows and dense data into interfaces people can understand and use confidently.
You're comfortable working in Figma with components, auto layout, and interactive prototypes, and applying accessibility and responsive design principles.
You can run focused customer conversations and usability sessions, explain tradeoffs, and work closely with engineers to ship a practical solution.
You take initiative, make progress when requirements are still forming, and care about the details of the finished product.

Experience designing cybersecurity, developer tools, or enterprise software.
Experience with data visualization, policy management, or investigation workflows.
Familiarity with AI agents and how they use tools and data.
Working knowledge of HTML and CSS, or experience building prototypes with code or AI tools.
Please include a portfolio link with your application.
What We Offer
We offer a competitive package for people who can move quickly, work with enterprise customers, and help build critical infrastructure for enterprise AI.
Competitive package. Salary, equity, and benefits aligned with the scope and ownership of the role.
Time off. Four weeks of paid vacation, paid sick leave, and paid parental leave.
Professional development. Budget for conferences, courses, and certifications across AI, enterprise software, and security.
Equipment. A MacBook and the equipment you need to do your best work.
Health benefits. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.
Retirement savings. 401(k) retirement plan.
Customer access. Work directly with companies adopting AI in production and see the impact of what you build.

About Novig
Novig is building America's #1 sports prediction market. Our mission is to financialize and democratize sports trading - taking a closed system run by casinos and turning it into a fair, efficient, two-sided market where the power sits with users.

With Novig recently becoming a CFTC-designated market — the fastest designation of its kind in US history— we're bringing the prediction market built for sports fans nationwide.

We're backed by some of Silicon Valley's top investors — Pantera, Forerunner, Lux, NFX, Paul Graham, and Joe Montana — who have collectively invested over $100M behind this vision.

About the Role
We’re hiring a Product Designer at Novig to help craft the core experience of the best sports prediction market in the world.

This is a high-ownership role with real scope, autonomy, and influence over the direction of the product. You'll work directly with the VP of Design, founder, and core product team, shaping the product end-to-end — from understanding users, concepting new product features, and helping frame product direction to shipping precise, polished interfaces.

Who you are and what you will do
You build what users love. You design experiences that feel intuitive, rewarding, and differentiated, deepening how fans engage with sports trading.

You make complexity feel simple. You turn sports markets, live data, and trading mechanics into clear, fast, and engaging product experiences.

You validate ideas fast. You rapidly concept, prototype, test, and iterate to produce the highest-impact solutions, pushing for the highest quality execution, thoughtful interaction design, and strong product thinking across every surface and flow.

You help evolve our system. You define, grow, and maintain our design system to keep our product cohesive as it grows.

You have 3–4+ years of product design experience, with a portfolio that shows system-level thinking, strong attention to detail, and tangible business impact — backed by excellent visual and interaction design skills and deep Figma fluency.

You have a sharp instinct for user behavior and what makes products click, with strong product judgment grounded in real customer understanding.

You have a strong point of view on design systems — you think in components, tokens, and variants.

You're AI-forward, with a strong interest in actively integrating AI into design workflows.

You move quickly and adapt well in fast-paced environments, with a bias toward ownership and action, clear and thoughtful communication, and genuine curiosity about markets.

Bonus: you have experience in fintech, sports betting, trading, or other data-rich consumer products.

Why work here, in the words of the people who do
“I work with extremely stellar people, I own real systems, and decisions happen fast. No politics, no waiting for needless red tape. If something's broken, I fix it. If I build something good, it ships.”

“The people! They're smart, thoughtful, fun to work with and passionate about their craft.”

“I'm having the most fun I've had in my entire career.”

If you want responsibility, trust, and the chance to help build the future of sports prediction markets - take your shot, we’d love to connect.

Not for everyone
Our work is tied to live sports - that means potential nights, weekends, and pressure included.

If you need clear swim lanes, a heavy process, or someone to tell you what to do, this won’t be the right environment.

ABOUT SCHOLARLY
Scholarly is building the next generation of AI-powered software for higher education with a faculty-first focus. As institutions face a wave of digital transformation, our mission is to become the AI-native system of record for faculty data.
Our platform unifies fragmented workflows into a single, intelligent system - powering annual reviews, promotion & tenure, appointment tracking, and more - while eliminating manual data entry and improving decision-making for institutions. We're a mission-driven, product-focused team shaping the future of higher education.
POSITION OVERVIEW
Scholarly is hiring its first full-time designer. As our Founding Product Designer, you'll own how Scholarly looks, feels, and works - from the data-dense screens administrators live in every day, to the faculty-facing experiences that need to just work, to the website and materials that introduce us to new institutions.
We're looking for a designer with 7 or more years of experience, including meaningful time shipping complex B2B or SaaS products. You'll work directly with engineering and leadership, and you'll be the person who sets up how design works at Scholarly: the system, the process, and the bar. You can read about how we work in this blog post https://kellysutton.com/2025/08/04/how-were-working-2025.html .
This role is based in Seattle and on-site with the engineering team in Pioneer Square.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Own product design end-to-end. Take features from fuzzy customer problem to shipped, polished experience - workflows, information architecture, interaction design, and visual design.

Build and own the Scholarly design system. Define the components, tokens, and patterns our frontend is built on, including the dense tables and grids that power faculty data management.

Talk to our users. Run interviews, usability tests, and site visits with faculty, department administrators, and faculty affairs teams at our customer institutions, and turn what you learn into product direction.

Prototype in code. You're comfortable in HTML and CSS - whether that's building a high-fidelity prototype, pairing with an engineer, or shipping a front-end polish fix yourself. Claude and other AI tools are your force multipliers.

Shape the brand. Lead design for our website, sales and demo materials, and the documents we put in front of prospective customers.

Guide product decisions. You'll have a real voice in what we build and why, not just how it looks.

QUALIFICATIONS
7 or more years of product design experience, with a portfolio that shows complex, workflow-heavy or data-dense products shipped to real users.

Experience building or significantly evolving a design system.

Hands-on user research experience - you've planned and run your own studies.

Working knowledge of front-end code (HTML, CSS).

Brand or marketing design experience is a strong plus.

Experience in higher education, healthcare, HR, or other enterprise/regulated software is a plus, but not required.

Authorized to work in the United States (citizen or green card holder). We're not able to sponsor visas at this time.

Excited to work on-site in Seattle 5 days per week.
